## The trace: 3 flows, 10 cross-flow findings

`Item.Name`, `Item.SellIn`, `Item.Quality` — all `pii_classification: none`, asserted only after sweeping for regulated identifiers and the FAA catalog (certificate number, FTN, MID, designee, N-Number, MedXPress/AME fields). All 22 citations verified line-by-line.

**Three implicit transformations** (this skill's core purpose — the peer artifact found zero):
- Null drift via the BCL's null-tolerant string equality, routing a null name into the wrong branch
- Default **unchecked** int arithmetic on the SellIn decrement — no floor, silent wrap at `int.MinValue`
- **Read-after-write aliasing**: Quality is decremented twice in one iteration; the second guard reads the value the first already mutated, so `-2` becomes `-1` at Quality 1

**The headline findings:**
- **Zero business-data egress.** `exit_points` is empty on all three flows — a verified property, not lazy tracing. The only `Console.WriteLine` emits `"OMGHAI!"` *before* the calculation. The app computes Quality and throws the answer away.
- **Only 2 of 7 Quality writes ever execute** under the shipped seeds. The post-sell-by block (83-109) is dead because no seed goes negative after the decrement, and the backstage accelerations are dead because the sole Backstage seed is SellIn 15. So a characterization test seeded from the existing item list would **pass while missing most of the rule set** — which is why I corrected the mitigation on the ordering-coupling finding to say the test set must be extended.
- **Read-write ordering coupling:** SellIn is read pre-decrement at lines 59/67 and post-decrement at 83. Moving the decrement — the most natural refactor — silently changes outcomes at SellIn 11, 6 and 0, with the only test asserting `Assert.True(true)`.

## One thing you should know about the artifact

The schema cannot express this result. It forbids the honest values: `image_count_estimate` has `minimum: 1` (true count is zero), `sample_size` has `minimum: 100` (zero sampled), every readiness score has `minimum: 1`, and four fields are closed enums with no not-applicable member. **The numbers in this file are sentinels, and they look exactly like measurements.** A scheduler reading them alone would believe a 1-image corpus was assessed at readiness 1 from a 100-image sample. The truth lives only in the prose fields and the 7 risk findings.

I flagged that as a `high` finding with a concrete contract fix: add a required `assessment_status` enum (`assessed | no-corpus-detected | blocked`) and relax the numeric minimums when status isn't `assessed`. Worth doing — this will recur on every not-applicable dispatch.
